scope: Theorem 5.1 (Rigidity at a small test scale) of the manuscript “The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale” (preprints/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 217 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e0e2e5e34169e701), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, every sequence has a subsequence on which, for some κ, r(xv) x −→ v κ locally uniformly for v ∈ (0, ∞), 0 < c ≤ κ ≤ C < ∞. (28) The bounds on κ depend only on T and the total-clock bounds. The same conclusion holds for a comparison with an omitted lower group, provided its changed paths and the constrained competitors used in the first variation are admissible.
